the development of an advanced ultrasonic testing (UT) system that can detect and characterize defects in the welds of nuclear power plant piping and vessels.
the application of phased-array ultrasonics for the inspection of austenitic stainless piping welds from the far-side.
the development of a new approach to the detection of corrosion and cracking in the heat-affected zone (HAZ) and weld of stainless steel piping.

the phased-array ultrasonic examination technique is an effective means to detect flaws and accurately size the length of flaws in austenitic stainless-steel piping welds, regardless of the welding technique.
both the longitudinal and shear wave probes were able to accurately length-size all flaws, but not depth-size all flaws, through these welds.
the phased-array ultrasonic inspection of austenitic welds can provide accurate length sizing of flaws through the weld, but cannot be used for accurate depth sizing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phased-array ultrasonic technique is capable of performing through weld flaw inspections in austenitic stainless piping and that it can provide accurate flaw length sizing, but not depth sizing.
the phased-array ultrasonic examination of the welds is a viable alternative to the current ASME Section XI, Appendix VIII “best effort” method of examination.
